(In the palace.)

@@U04536@@
Four of them came, three have left. I made no sense of what they said. Some echoing word like “breath,” and then a rhyme sounding like “death.” A dismal word. Hollow, muffled, a sigh so ghostly. Ah, why have I not won my way to freedom? Why? Into the open? To Nature? Why? Not stripped myself of magic, unlearned all incantations? Forever! And stand before you, Nature— a man— only a man! Then, ah, then it would be worthwhile to be human. I was that once, before I plumbed the depths of darkness, damning the world and myself with evil blasphemies, the world that is now so thronged with phantoms and specters that there is no escape. Daylight may be sweet, hours of sun and sanity; and then night comes and trammels us in a net of dreams. Home we wend from a happy springtime romp in the fields, and a bird croaks. And what does it croak?

@@U04535@@
（在宫殿里。）

@@U04536@@
四个人来了，三个人走了。我没听懂他们说的话。一些类似“呼吸”的回声词，然后是听起来像“死亡”的押韵。一个凄凉的词。空洞、低沉、阴森的叹息。啊，为什么我没有赢得自由？为什么？进入公开状态？走向自然？为什么？没有剥夺自己的魔法，忘记所有的咒语？永远！站在你面前，大自然——一个人——只是一个人！那么啊，那就值得做人了。我曾经就是这样，在我探索黑暗的深处，用邪恶的亵渎诅咒世界和我自己之前，这个世界现在充满了幻影和幽灵，无处可逃。白天可能是甜蜜的，阳光明媚，神智清醒；然后夜幕降临，把我们困在梦之网中。我们在春天的田野里快乐地嬉戏，回家时听到一只鸟儿呱呱叫。它发出什么声音？
